tools.name: windows_list
tools.title: Open windows
tools.description: The windows open on this desktop, the most recently used first: address, app, title, workspace ("background" for an app hidden in the background), whether it has the focus and whether it is on screen now. A window Send to Claude leaves out (a password manager, a private browser window, an app the user listed) is there as private, without its title. Use the address to name the window to the other window tools.

tools.name: windows_view
tools.title: See a window
tools.description: A picture of one window as it is on screen now, to read what it shows (a page, a document, an error). Only a window on screen: one that isn't must be brought forward first. The user is usually asked on screen first, with the app and the window's title (not for the apps they let you see without asking), so take one picture of what you need rather than several. Never of a window Send to Claude leaves out (password managers, private browser windows, the apps the user listed), nor with one of those over it; that is the user's choice, so don't try another way.

window.description: Its address (the list of open windows has them), or an app's name (its most recently used window)

tools.name: windows_focus
tools.title: Bring a window forward
tools.description: Brings a window forward and gives it the focus, switching to its workspace (one hidden in the background comes to the current one). Not while the user is typing: it waits a few seconds for a pause, then refuses, so what they type doesn't go to another window. Then try again a little later, or ask them.

window.description: Its address from windows_list, or an app's name (its most recently used window)

tools.name: apps_open
tools.title: Open an app
tools.description: Opens an app, as the Launcher does, by its name ("Firefox", "Files") or desktop id (org.gnome.Nautilus); one that is already open is brought forward instead. An unclear name returns the apps it could mean. Only the Launcher's apps, without arguments: open a file with files_open, an address with open_address. Not while the user is typing, as windows_focus.

app.description: The app's name or desktop id

tools.name: open_address
tools.title: Open an address
tools.description: Opens a web address (http, https) in the default browser, or a mailto: link in the mail app's composer (nothing is sent). Opening an address sends it to that site, so the user allows it on screen first. Not while the user is typing, as windows_focus.

tools.name: files_recent
tools.title: Recent files
tools.description: The newest files in the user's Downloads, Pictures and Documents (and folders three levels below them) that are in the folders the user lets Claude use, newest first: path, name, folder, size in bytes, modified (ISO 8601) and type. Use it for "the PDF I just downloaded" or "my last screenshot". Hidden files are left out.

name.description: Only names with this text in them (any case)

tools.name: files_open
tools.title: Open a file
tools.description: Opens a file or folder in the user's home folder in its default app (a PDF in the viewer, a folder in Files). Only documents, pictures, sound, video, text and folders: never a program, a script or a launcher, nor anything hidden (no part of the path starting with a dot), outside home or outside the folders the user lets Claude use (a link counts where it points). Not while the user is typing, as windows_focus.

path.description: An absolute path, or one relative to home (~ works too)

tools.name: files_trash
tools.title: Move to the trash
tools.description: Moves files or folders in the user's home folder to the trash, where Files shows them and can put them back; nothing is deleted for good (there is no tool for that). Not home's own folders (Downloads, Documents…), nothing hidden, nothing outside home or the folders the user lets Claude use. Several paths go together: all or none. The user is usually asked on screen first, with every path and how many files each folder holds, so trash what belongs together in one call.

paths.description: Absolute paths, or relative to home
